decision: Treat done as three checks: c8 reports 100 and fails under it, published src stays at 0 dependencies and does not grow its gzip size, and uncontended createLock acquire plus release gets faster than the measured baseline without slowing the queue
why: The README claims a small tested toolkit. The speed claim is only true if a frozen command can show it.

decision: c8 already reports 100 percent statements, branches, functions, and lines on src, but npm test does not fail when that drops
why: A green suite that does not check the threshold can ship a coverage hole.

decision: Published runtime is 6788 bytes across four files, 2293 bytes gzipped together, and zero runtime dependencies
why: Minimal means the files npm ships, not the docs site.

decision: Uncontended createLock median is 130.89 ms for 1e6 acquire-release pairs, range 129.46-179.95, 0 errors, 7 processes. async-sema median is 105.10 ms. A cached resolved promise median is 95.16 ms. The await floor median is 91.17 ms.
why: Each acquire currently builds a new promise. The profile ticks sit in microtasks and GC. The queue burst median is 52.31 ms for 400000 grants and overlaps the cached variant.

decision: Fail npm test when src coverage drops below 100 percent on statements, branches, functions, or lines
why: The suite was already at 100 percent. The missing piece was a gate. An unused function in create.js made c8 exit 1, and removing it made npm test exit 0.

decision: Return the same resolved promise from createLock when a slot is free and no signal was passed
why: Every free acquire was allocating a promise. A profile of the old path sat in microtasks and GC. The await of an already resolved promise is the floor, median 90.27 ms, and the new path median is 96.16 ms, so the lock body is no longer most of the time.

decision: Left the fair queue and withLock wrapper alone
why: A promise-resolve shortcut on the fair queue moved the median from 39.88 ms to 38.18 ms for 200000 acquires, and the ranges overlapped. A thinner withLock was slower on async functions, median 33.84 ms against 33.18 ms. It was faster only for a sync callback, which is not the call shape the README shows.

decision: Supersede the 135.09 ms to 96.16 ms pair. Those runs caught errors inside the timed loop. The clean loop, median of 7 processes, 0 errors, is 80.45 ms before and 43.31 ms after for 1e6 acquires. async-sema median is 64.40 ms. The await floor is 38.07 ms.
why: A try/catch on every acquire was part of the earlier number. Both sides paid it, and the clean loop is the one a caller runs.

decision: Queue drain median is 58.81 ms before and 57.37 ms after for 400000 grants. Ranges overlap.
why: The fast path does not run once the slot count hits zero, so the queue should not move.

decision: Gzip of the four runtime files went from 2293 bytes to 2323 bytes
why: The free-slot promise is one more binding. A fair-queue shortcut and a thinner withLock did not earn their bytes.

decision: AsyncLocalStorage still saw caller 1 then caller 2 around a contended createLock
why: A shared promise can resume in the wrong async context. The new lock kept each caller in its own store.

decision: A reviewer reruns the current tree with node benchmark/index.js. On this machine that printed createLock free median 41.2 ms for 1e6 acquires and 0 errors. The before and after pair lives in the measure rows above. The /tmp scripts are not in the repo.
why: The isolated before and after runs are the comparison. The in-repo bench is the current tree only, and its 41.2 ms sits next to the isolated after median of 43.31 ms.

decision: Left createLock double-release as it was. A second call still adds a slot. Fair queue still ignores a second release.
why: A per-acquire guard would allocate the closure the free path just stopped allocating.
